all.notes:
Unit A, topic tension capacity. 282 probes run on the untouched ext/ tree (nothing under /home/user/1 modified). Verdicts: 115 right, 77 wrong, 44 stopped, 24 asked, 13 hidden, 5 partial, 4 warned. All 36 reported hits are CLEAN (status answered, no UNKNOWN WORDS, no warning line). Each was re-run from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-1/a6672620-4f5b-5cfe-8fc0-05cb48074075/scratchpad/A/tcap/hits.json (output rh.json), and each right value was checked by hand with her method. Most also fire in his style (misspellings, glued commas) and several in clean exam wording (c01, c03, c04, c05, c08, c11).

Root causes, most dangerous first:
1. A scoped negation becomes "the whole member is welded" (hits 01-08). reader.js tensionCommon has `if (/no\s+bolt\s+holes/i.test(t)) welded = true` with no condition, and the weldedWord regex matches "no holes" in "no holes in the web". So "no bolt holes in the web / in the flanges / the short leg has no bolt holes / no bolt holes elsewhere" all print the no-holes yielding value. This is ordinary exam wording. One fix closes 8 hits.
2. The count regexes skip across a comma and a "no" (hits 09-11). `(WN) lines of (?:\S+\s+){0,5}? bolts ... the web` reads "four lines of 3/4in bolts, no holes in the web" as 4 WEB holes, and the connection becomes 'all' (U 1.0).
3. Asked quantity without an asking verb, or one that ASK_WORDS does not list (hits 21, 24-33). These answer with the capacity:
   - "design strength for yielding?", "yield strength?", "gross yielding?"
   - "find the rupture strength", "fracture strength?", "net section rupture?", "phi Pn for rupture"
   - "nominal (tensile) strength", "Pn", "nominal yield strength"
   - "L/r?" / "slenderness ratio?"
   - an Ae ask on a welded member
   "nominal tensile strength" is even matched AS a phipn ask through "tensile strength". With "find ... for yielding" the page answers correctly, so the gap is the prose detector (asksInProse needs a verb; the limit-state rewrite needs an existing phipn ask).
4. Counts:
   - Double angles named any way except "double angle(s)", "two angles", "pair of angles", "2L", "2-L", "2 L": one angle is used (hits 12-13).
   - "through both legs" for an angle: 1 hole and Case 8 instead of 2 holes and U 1.0 (14-16).
   - A BOLT count per flange is taken as holes across the flange (17).
   - "one line ... on each side of the web in each flange" gives 1 per flange (18).
5. Glued typing ("3/4inbolts", "2holes") skips both the bolt reader and the "you mention bolts or holes" guard, so the page prints the no-holes 702 (hit 19). Related design point: "W12x53 tension member find phi Pn" with no word about the connection also prints 702 (no holes assumed silently) instead of asking bolted or welded (probe Po17).
6. Loads:
   - A number without its own unit is dropped silently: "D=100, L=150 kips", "D=100k,L=150", "dead 100 live 150 kips". The adequacy verdict flips to "adequate" (hits 34-36). The unused-number gate only sees numbers that carry units.
   - Working typed along: "Pu = 1.2(100) + 1.6(150)" is read as Pu = 1.2 (hit 20).
   - "max service live load if D = 100k" makes up L = 100 (hit 21).
7. Hole versus bolt: "holes 7/8 in diameter" / "The holes are 15/16 in. in diameter" are taken as BOLT sizes (findBolt pattern 4 forces kind 'bolt'). Wrong under every reading (hits 22-23).

Avoidable stops and hides, not hits:
- "thru" is an UNKNOWN word. It hid 13 probes, every answer of each. Two of those hidden answers are also wrong (Pm10 U 0.80 for 1.0, Pm24 An 4.29 for 8.58), so fix the hits before unhiding "thru".
- "not staggered" / "no stagger" trigger the stagger stop (Pp13, Pq26, Pn16; no negation in the H.stagger regex).
- "3-4in" and "3 /4 in" are read as a 4 in bolt and stop.
- "check L/r" and "max factored load it can carry?" ask for a load.
- "Tu =", "factored tension 380k", "P = 120 kips factored", loads in lb, and unit-less "D=100 L=150" all ask.
- Multiple choice with kips options asks about the unused numbers instead of circling.
- "web isn't bolted" / "web not bolted" / "not connected through the web" ask for web holes.
- "four bolts in each flange" (no lines) asks for the per-line count (good).
- Two lettered problems in one box: (b) "same member welded" is lost silently (Pt22).

Other notes:
- engine.js line 469 (frozen): the AMBIGUOUS stop for any unequal 2L (e.g. 2L4x3x3/8) says "For tension use the single angle (L8X4X1/2) and set angles to 2". That is a hard-coded example shape, wrong for this member, inside a stop message. He may type it. Route around it in pipeline.
- Ambiguous but chosen silently:
  - "bolted through its flanges with two lines of bolts" is halved to 1 per flange (u02: 640.3; 596.2 if it means two lines in each flange). This matches the May 2024 final convention.
  - "six bolts in 3 rows of 2" on a plate is read as 3 holes across (t11).
- The calculator's angle U counts ALL fasteners (her HW 3-26 reading). The AISC per-line warning shows only in the read lines.
- Label numbers (problem numbers, points, "Fig 3-4", "hw 3-26", "Q4 (15pts)") were never read as data.

Scratch files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-1/a6672620-4f5b-5cfe-8fc0-05cb48074075/scratchpad/A/tcap/ holds the probe sets (p1-p10.json, oneoffs.json), runs (r*.json), hits.json/rh.json, probes-final.json, the independent key calculator key.js and the box dumper boxes.js.

all.notes:
I ran 232 probes on tools/steel-tool-solve/ext. The results were 92 right, 60 wrong, 31 stopped, 29 asked, 9 warned, 5 hidden and 6 partial. The 36 minimal hits all reproduce byte-for-byte on the untouched baseline $SP/base-src, so no worker edit caused them. All hits are clean (no ALSO FOUND / NOT WHAT / CHECK / UNKNOWN marker on the line). Scratch files are in $SP/A/tsel/: key.js is an independent selector that uses the frozen data only (her method); final.json / final.out.json hold the hits; r1..r17.json hold the probes.

ROOT CAUSES, most dangerous first:

1. LOAD-0 (hits 01-08 plus probes q01-q08, s10, s15, t08, t11-t15, p83, c09). This is the most likely to hit him. A dead or live load that the reader does not read becomes 0, because engine loadFromArgs does D = hasD ? a.D : 0, and nothing stops it.
   - Missed when the unit is typed once for the pair: "D=50 L=100 kips", "D = 40, L = 90 kips", "service loads D=50 and L=100 kips", "dead load 50 and live load 100 kips", "L=100 kips D=50".
   - Missed when only the first value has a unit: "D=50k L=100", "D=50 kips L=100", "D=50k, L=100".
   - Missed in ratios and equalities: "twice the dead load", "L=2D", "L = D", "D = L = 75 kips", "each 50 kips", "equal dead and live loads of 75 k".
   - Step 1 prints "1.2 (0)" or "1.4D governs", and nobody reading would notice. It flips both the selected shape and YES/NO.
   - PD=50 PL=100k is read correctly, and "D = 50 k L = 100 k" works. The gap is specific to bare D/L with a shared unit. The unused-number gate ignores numbers without a unit.
   - Suggested guard: if the text names dead and live (D=, L=, dead, live, DL, LL) and only one box holds a value, or a ratio word ties them, stop. Optionally carry a trailing kips back to an unread "D=50" in the same pair.
   - This is also a NEW path to the known 1.4D issue: a dropped L makes 1.4D govern (hits 03, 05, 09).

2. NO-HOLES (hits 10-12, probes v12, w06, c04). These are bolted members computed with no holes, which gives yielding only and a lighter shape.
   - Triggers: "bolted 3/4in 2 per flange 3 per line" (the noun "bolts" is missing), and his glued "3/4inbolts 2perflange 3perline".
   - The bolt size sits in read.unused but the gate never asks. Only a read NOTE ("no holes were entered") appears.
   - Suggested guard: if the text contains bolt, bolted or hole(s) and every hole box is empty, stop.

3. LENGTH (hits 14-16, probes t01-t03, t06, u03, u04, u07-u09, u11). The member length is not placed, so tension_select skips L/r <= 300 and picks a too-slender shape.
   - Triggers: "L = 25 ft" (the L symbol collides with live load), a bare "25ft", "25 ft. long", "unbraced length 25 ft", "spans 25 ft between joints", "KL = 25 ft", "length 2 5 ft".
   - read.unused holds the length, but tension_select raises no ask. Only a read NOTE appears.

4. ASKED QUANTITY in a sentence with no blank (hits 23-29). The capacity line is printed as ANSWER for:
   - excess capacity, extra load, "how much more factored load", "by how much does the strength exceed the load";
   - percent used;
   - nominal Pn, nominal rupture;
   - "design strength for yielding": the 10/06 class, still open in the no-blank form;
   - ASD allowable.
   The blank forms of these are already caught (CHECK YOUR BLANK / NOT WHAT YOUR BLANK ASKS). The qualifier list of the blank path should also apply to askedInWords.

5. MAX family (hits 30-35). The reader max_load regex needs the full word "maximum".
   - Not chained: "max service live load?", "max. live load", "maximum LL", "maximum total service load".
   - "maximum service dead load" (L given) and "live load = 2 x dead load, max dead load?" have no stage at all.
   - Each prints phi Pn as ANSWER. With "maximum ... live load" the chain works and is right.
   - In every chained max-live-load question, the ANSWER (step 1) line also prints "adequate for Pu = 56". That is 1.4D with the unknown L set to 0: a second number on a copy line, and a new place where the known 1.4D issue reaches a printed line.

6. REQUIRED-AREA family (hits 18-22, probes p07, p15, p62, z02, z04, z07). These print Ag, or the selected shape's Ag, for asks such as:
   - "required net area" and "minimum net area required";
   - "required Ae";
   - "Ag required = ____" (a blank line is filled with the shape's Ag 5.26 instead of 4.889);
   - "min Ag?";
   - "required area" in a select question.
   Hit 09: "live load 3 times the dead load" plus "required gross area" is routed to loads_factored, which prints a factored load.

7. Smaller items.
   - Self-weight: "include self weight" is ignored in tension questions (hit 36; p23 shows a wrong Pu on the line).
   - Lines in flanges: "2 lines of bolts in/through the flanges" is silently read as 1 per flange (hit 13; two readings, so it should ask).
   - L/r verdict: "is it adequate" says YES while the page's own step says L/r 355 > 300 TOO SLENDER (hit 17). Whether this counts depends on whether she treats 300 as pass/fail. Her select form does.

STOPS AND ASKS THAT LOOK AVOIDABLE, all of them safe:
- "thru" is an UNKNOWN WORD and hides right answers (p01, p85, b06). It is very common in his typing and is worth adding as a known word.
- "tensionmember" (glued) also hides answers.
- Factored loads not written as "factored load"/"Pu =" become "number in no box" asks: "Tu = 200 kips", "tensile load of 200 kips", "220 kips factored", "already factored", "factored tension 130 kips", "factored dead load 60k and factored live load 160k".
- "DL = 50k LL = 100k", "D.L.", "dead = 50k live = 100k" and capital "50K" all become asks.
- "maximum factored load the member can carry" asks for a load it does not need (p70).
- A count followed by a fraction ("one line of 4 3/4in bolts", "4 7/8in") is read as 4.75 / 4.875 and stopped by the plausibility check. Safe, but it is a common phrasing.
- "3 /4" and "3-4" are read as 4 and stopped.
- Two shapes in one text ("W12x26 beam hangs from a W8x18 hanger", "the w8x21 failed, check a w8x24") are refused with an unrelated plate/holes message.
- "(none in the web) 7/8in bolts 4 per line" lost the count per line (p46).
- Channel select with web bolts is refused (needs Case 2). That is correct.

CHECKED AND SAFE: problem numbers, point values, figure numbers and HW labels are never read as data (x01-x10, p10, p33, p34, p49). The book's answer typed along is ignored (p58, c06). "not welded", "not bolted, it is welded", "no web holes" and "none in the web" are all handled.

all.notes:
I ran 316 probes on the cloud tree. Results: 118 right, 85 stopped, 84 wrong, 10 warned, 8 hidden, 8 partial, 3 asked. The 84 wrong probes come from about 15 root causes. The 35 hits are those causes cut down to minimal texts: 31 clean-wrong, 2 wrong-under-warning, 2 wrong-hidden. Every page_line was checked by re-running the hit text, and every table value came from harness/lookup.js. Scratch files are in $SP/A/ccap: q*.json and r*.json are the runs; probes.json and hits.json are this output.

PATTERNS (most dangerous first)
1. findBracing in reader.js is the weakest part of the column reader. It produces six separate kinds of clean-wrong answer:
   (a) It reads no axis words. Any mid-height brace goes to Ly. This catches "about the strong axis", "about the x axis", "x-x axis", "in the strong direction", "in the plane of the web" and "strong axis but not the weak". W10x45 prints 460 against a right value of 209, 2.2 times unconservative.
   (b) It ignores negation: "not braced at mid height", "unbraced at mid height", "no bracing at mid-height", and "bracing ... is removed", where the negation comes after the noun.
   (c) "1/3 points" is read as mid-height. "third" is never in "1/3", so w falls through to 2.
   (d) For "at 10 ft and 20 ft from the base" it keeps only one height.
   (e) When the weak axis is braced at the third points and the strong axis at mid height, it keeps one brace only.
   (f) The useSeg branch (a brace at a height above the base) gives every segment the whole column's end condition. This goes against her rule as written in reader.js's own 0.5 comment: an end segment keeps its end, the other segments are pinned-pinned. Fixed-pinned gets K 0.8 on the pinned segment; fixed-fixed gets 0.65 where 0.8 is right. The mid-height case through segRows is right.
   A related slip: when Lx and Ly are typed with a fixed end, the end K is applied to the braced Ly. The same column described in words gets a different answer.
2. The Euler form is wrong whenever anything beyond "pinned ends, one length" is typed. The reader does ask euler_K for non-pinned ends, but the K box has an engine default of 1 and is not required, so the ask never gates. The page then prints a clean Pcr with K = 1 for fixed-fixed, fixed-pinned and flagpole columns (flagpole: 185 printed, 42 right). It also ignores a mid-height brace, a named strong axis (it always uses min r) and a typed E. A minimal fix is to stop the Euler form whenever an end condition other than pinned, a brace, an axis word, or "E =" appears.
3. Prose questions that ask for something other than the form's headline get the headline as the ANSWER:
   - "nominal strength" or a bare "find Pn" / "what is Pn" gets phi Pn. The blank "Pn = ____" is handled right, so the fix is to reuse SIG_NOMINAL for prose.
   - "allowable strength" gets phi Pn.
   - "effective length" gets the factor K.
   - "euler critical stress" or "critical buckling stress" gets the load Pcr. The typo "whats" also defeats asksInProse.
   - "KL/r about the x axis" or "slenderness ratio about the strong axis" gets the governing value.
   - "using table 4-14" or "from Table 4-1a" gets the other table's value. The gap is only 1%, but the named table is ignored.
   - "use phi = 0.85" is silently dropped.
4. Form choice: Kx/Ky together with "find phi Pn", without the word "column" ("member", "col."), goes to TENSION and prints 648 for a 527 column.
5. Two printed K values with axis words ("K = 0.8 about x and K = 1.0 about y") are both read as the first K. With "pinned ends" also in the text, the printed Kx is silently dropped.
6. Loads:
   - "Pu = 1.2(100) + 1.6(150)" is read as Pu = 1.2, which gives a false YES for W12x40.
   - "find the max service live load, dead load = 100 kips" takes the 100 for both D and L. The page answers phi Pn with an invented Pu of 280 and never gives the asked live load of 170. This is a new route of the known gap: answered, not stopped.
   - With "if the dead load is 100 kips" the max-live-load chain is added and its answer (170) is right, but the step-1 ANSWER line still states the invented Pu = 280.
7. Two lettered parts: "(b) repeat if it is braced at mid height ..." is sent to the definitions finder, and a class quote is printed as part (b)'s ANSWER.
8. Unknown-word hiding catches some of these only by luck ("midheight", "theory", "colu"). Once he confirms the spelling, the wrong value shows.

AVOIDABLE STOPS (not hits, but they cost coverage)
- A bare "pinned" without "ends" after the length ("20 ft long pinned, D=..."; "30 ft, pinned.") is not read as an end condition.
- A length without "long" or "L =" is often missed: "pinned ends 16ft.", "12 ft free at top", "18 ft pinned both ends", "16 ft pinned ends find", "HSS8x8x1/2 column 16 ft pinned ends".
- End conditions not read: "fixed both ends" (no "at"), "one end pinned one end fixed", "pinned-fixed", "built in at both ends", "one end fixed and the other end free", "top restrained against rotation but free to translate".
- "Kx = 1.0, Ky = 0.8" with the word column stops (Kx/Ky not read).
- Other lengths and braces not read: "1/4 points", "every 7 ft", "braced at 2 points", "no lateral bracing", "weak axis unbraced length 12 ft", "16 ft effective length about the x axis and 8 ft about the y axis" (page stop).
- Other asks the page cannot answer: "find Fcr" / "critical stress Fcr" (no phi), the slenderness-limit check, "maximum unbraced length for KL/r = 200", "max slenderness allowed" (200), "factored load capacity", and "recommended design value of K ... other end free".

SILENT ASSUMPTIONS (conventional; noted only)
- "braced at mid height" with no axis is taken as the weak axis.
- Euler with no end condition takes K = 1.
- An HP12x53 slender flange gets a read WARNING only.
- A whole-foot KL row is used for Table 4-1a when KL is not a whole number (rounded up).

SEEN RIGHT
K lookups; Table 4-1a vs 4-14 routing; Fy 36 / 65 / A36 through Table 4-14; HSS (her Fy 50), pipe (Fy 35), HP; W shapes with slender webs; KxLx/KyLy in either order; "Lx = 12" with a total length; "3rd points", "quarter points", "both directions"; braces "10 ft from the bottom" and "14 ft from the top" on pinned-pinned columns; a mid-height brace on fixed-fixed columns; 13'-6", 168 in, "14 ft 6 in", "K = .8", "KL=14'"; label numbers ("(10 pts)", "problem 4.3", "HW 5-17", "fig 4-12", "Example 4.2", "3)"); the book answer typed along; D/L loads and conflicting Pu (asks); two lettered columns; the blanks "Pn = ____" and "KL = ____"; "which axis governs"; the round bar in Euler.

all.notes:
I found 26 hits; every one is a clean ANSWER line that is wrong by her method. I worked each answer by hand from the frozen data, using my own script for her method (scratch/A/csel/her.js). Several hits pick a section that is too small, so a student copying them would be unsafe: A1-csel-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 07, 08, 09, 10.

Patterns:

1) A misread number slips through when one form passes its result to the next. When the load takedown feeds column selection, the unused-number check goes quiet. SOLVE.unusedOf counts a number as used if ANY stage's reader took it, even though column_select's D and L boxes are replaced by the Pu carried over from the takedown. The same text with "find factored load" (takedown alone) asks "which box does 100 psf belong in?"; the chained text answers wrong. Hits: 08, 09, 10, R08, S14, R13. Add that the floor dead box (floor_D_psf) and live boxes (floor_L_psf, L) quietly default to 0.

2) Empty L is treated as 0 (rule 1 broken). "L = 2D", "twice the dead load", "3 times dead", "equal to the dead load" and "dead load 200 kips and a live load" all give L = 0. That then sends Pu down the 1.4D path. Hits: 05, 06, 07.

3) The bracing reader (findBracing) handles neither negation nor axis, and keeps only one brace. "not braced / unbraced / no brace / without bracing at mid height" still halves Ly (03). "about its strong axis" goes to Ly (04). Braces at 10 ft and 20 ft keep only one (19). When "midheight" is typed as one word, the same wrong answer is only hidden under UNKNOWN WORDS (P11, X11, R20, Q25), so confirming the spelling reveals it.

4) Slash pairs are read as a fraction: "D/L = 200/300" gives 0.667, and "dead/live = 80/50 psf" gives 1.6 psf (01, 02).

5) carryAcross between lettered parts copies boxes from (a) even when (b) states its own value: a length the reader did not take ("effective length 25 ft", "KL 25 ft", "KL of 25 ft"), or "2 floors" (12, 13).

6) Fallback to loads_factored answers the wrong quantity. When column_select or the takedown cannot fill its boxes, the page prints "ANSWER: Factored load: 500 kips (already factored)" or "Factored load: 176 psf" for a "select the lightest W12" or "column load" question. Triggers seen:
   - lower-case "kxlx=kyly=14ft"
   - "Lx=24ft, Ly=12ft"
   - "Kx=1 Ky=1"
   - glued "3floors"
   - "3-story", "three-story", "3 stories", "3 storey building"
   - no floor count at all
   - part (b) with "L=25 ft"
   - bare "lightest w14 Pu=900k"
   Hits: 20, 21, 22, 23. The floor-count regex in reader.js (around line 747) needs whitespace between number and word, does not accept a hyphen, and misses "stories". Per-floor loads given in kips also ignore the floor count (14).

7) The guard for "load at a level that is not the lowest" misses "just below the roof", "under the roof", "between the 2nd and 3rd floors" and "from the 3rd floor to the roof" (17, 18, X36).

8) Other single findings:
   - "factored loads D=.. L=.." or "(factored)" gets factored a second time (11).
   - "N story building" plus a roof is read as roof + N floors (16).
   - Unequal adjacent bays: the first bay is used (15).
   - "50k snow" is dropped silently by the all-7-combinations form (24). By her single combination 360 / W12X50 would match, but the page claims to include snow.
   - A roof-live takedown chain prints the all-7-combinations step-1 ANSWER, with psf values used as kips, before stopping (25).
   - A select question with no member word goes silently to tension_select (26). Lower confidence: he may simply drop the word "column".

Things that are not hits but worth fixing:
- Spelling repair turns "sqft" into "sqrt" (S12), which loses the tributary area (a stop).
- After the roof ask, an unread floor count becomes floors = 0 and gives a roof-only answer under a CHECK note in the read block (S08, R24).
- Equal-weight tie across families (Pu 380, KL 12: W10X45 vs W12X45, both 45 lb/ft). The page silently prints W10X45 with a generic NOTE; her tie rule only exists for beams.

Stops that look avoidable:
- "KL 25 ft", "KL of 15 ft", "effective length 20 ft", "effective length is 16 ft about both axes"
- "fixed at base free at top", "both ends are fixed", "Kx = 1.0, Ky = 0.8"
- "14 ft between floors", "600 square ft", "an area of 25 ft x 30 ft"
- "dead 80 psf live 50 psf" with no comma (asks), "DL = 80 psf, LL = 50 psf" (asks)
- lower-case "roof: dead.. live.." sentences: the sentence cut requires an upper-case letter.

Label numbers were never read as data. I tried "problem 6.12 (10 pts)", "(15pts)", "fig 4.3", "hw 6-15 (20 points)", "6-7b)", "6-17", "3)", "(problem 3, 10 points)", "(ans. W12x72)" and "W14x82 phi Pn = 726" typed along; all were clean.

Known items, not re-reported: the 1.4D rule reaches the column ANSWER line through dead-only loads and changes the chosen shape (P07: her W12X50, page W12X53), and Q18 (takedown 262.5 vs 225). The bracketed alternative numbers I ignored.
